name: Ashwall Ironblood Territory Duster
description:
A knee-length duster in sun-bleached oxblood synth-canvas, hand-stenciled with the Ashwall Ironblood gang's territorial grid-map across the back in matte black and chrome-flake paint. Each panel carries layered patches: heat-stamped block numerals marking district claims, hand-sewn fabric swatches cut from defeated rivals, and reinforced shoulder yokes where chrome arm-rigs rest. Seams are triple-stitched in red monofilament. No two are identical — new patches added after each territorial dispute, making the coat a living record of violence and loyalty.

The interior lining is salvaged reflective emergency foil stitched into a crude quilt, offering marginal warmth against Shelf acid-rain while maintaining the silhouette.
functionality: Reinforced shoulder channels accommodate chrome arm prosthetics; interior foil lining provides acid-rain moisture resistance; deep inner pockets sized for contraband or medkits.
what_it_says: This coat is a walking deed of ownership — wearing it without permission is a death sentence.
price_range: Not for sale — earned or taken
story_hooks: A runner finds one of these coats on a body in neutral territory — wearing it to cross the district might work, or might start a war.
A patch on the back lists coordinates that don't match any known Shelf grid — someone sewed a dead-drop location into the gang's own iconography.
A Tier 3 fashion curator offers a small fortune for one as 'authentic subcultural artifact,' not understanding what it costs to own it.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A weathered, statement-making knee-length duster that reads as both armor and trophy. The silhouette is deliberately imposing—broad shoulders, straight lines, with visible wear that transforms it into a visual résumé of territorial conflict. The garment commands attention and signals dangerous allegiance.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, oversized through the torso to accommodate chrome arm-rigs; reinforced shoulder yokes create subtle structural rigidity. Cut for movement and layering, not tailored precision. The duster hangs with intentional swagger.
physical_description.primary_material: Sun-bleached oxblood synth-canvas—a durable, weather-resistant synthetic with a flat, utilitarian finish. Individual patches incorporate salvaged fabric, chrome-flake paint, and reflective emergency foil lining.
physical_description.texture: Mixed tactile experience: rough, canvas base with smooth painted sections, embossed numerals, stitched fabric overlays, and crinkled reflective interior. Matte black and chrome-flake accents add visual dimension. Triple red monofilament seams are visible and deliberate.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant oxblood red (faded and sun-scorched), accented with matte black territorial grid-map across the back, chrome-flake paint highlights, red monofilament stitching, and salvaged fabric patches of varied heritage colors. The reflective interior foil catches light unpredictably.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty industrial snap closures down the front; likely magnetic reinforced at stress points. No zippers—they corrode in acid rain. Utilitarian, durable, gang-standard.
distinctive_features: Hand-stenciled Ashwall Ironblood territorial grid-map (full back panel)
Heat-stamped district-claim numerals on each panel
Layered fabric patches from defeated rivals (hand-sewn trophy markers)
Reinforced chrome arm-rig yokes on shoulders
Triple red monofilament seaming (visible, intentional stitching)
Salvaged reflective emergency foil quilted lining
Unique modification history—new patches added after each territorial dispute
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade/ungoverned. This is salvage-culture elevated to cultural armor. It signals no corporate affiliation, no legitimate commerce—pure street hierarchy and violent reclamation.
physical_description.cultural_context: Gang infrastructure. Wearing this marks you as Ashwall Ironblood territory, a combatant or sworn affiliate. It's a literal map of conflicts and loyalties. The wearer is announcing themselves as dangerous, territorial, and loyal to the collective. Each patch is a story of violence survived or inflicted.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately weathered and patched. Pristine condition would suggest unworn status—authenticity demands visible wear, new stains, added patches from recent disputes, sun-fading, and acid-rain staining. The coat ages in real-time as the wearer's reputation grows.
